findings.reason: the arm must name an unbuilt case (the metered-lane queue) as the arm, or §5 must state the override is reused and drop it.
findings.text: §5's second case ("a local request with a priority override launches ahead of an earlier local request without one") is already implemented: priorities_first at reckon/crew/admission/ordering.py:106-146 hoists every request carrying queue_order._override (reckon/crew/queue_order.py:240-241, pointer key priority_override, written by `crew queue reprioritise`) ahead of the rest of the lane, _project_rank disambiguates by the same override at queue_order.py:333-339 and 360-361, and queued_placements reports it at ordering.py:259-265. That case cannot fail at base, which is the one thing a done-when arm must do.

findings.reason: §6 is left with only the seat-share rule, so it should state the delivered-review head is reused and reduce the section to the unbuilt share.
findings.text: §6's "among reviews the review of a delivered run goes first" also already ships: _is_review_run is the run-role classifier (reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:45), _project_rank sorts reviews ahead at reckon/crew/queue_order.py:336, admission_order_details names the reason "delivered review" at queue_order.py:356-357, and priorities_first keeps a delivered review at the head of the lane at ordering.py:143-146.

findings.reason: the endpoint is "a share", and the design must say one interleaver carries both dimensions rather than two that fight.
findings.text: §6's per-role seat share is a weighted interleaving of one ordered list by a key, which weighted_project_order already does for project weights (deficit round robin, ordering.py:70-103, applied at ordering.py:169-172 and 247-250). A second interleaver over roles, applied after the project one, reorders what the first established and can take seats from the deep project the weights exist to protect — reintroducing cross-project starvation as an unnamed regression.

findings.reason: §8 should state the pane depth derives from the existing place reader and index; a second census makes the pane the second ordering.
findings.text: §8's fleet-wide queue depth has two existing owners: queued_placements is documented as the one ordering every place-reporting surface reads so two surfaces "do not come to disagree about which request goes first" (ordering.py:199-207), and the per-project run census §8 wants is the open_run_index sqlite read (reckon/crew/open_run_index.py:397 read_rows) that the admission pass already wraps for operational reads (open_run_index.py:61).

findings.reason: the section should name one bounded pass reporting per-launch cost from the existing stage split; a parallel timer would double-count the same seconds.
findings.text: §7's per-launch duration and §7's pass budget both extend instruments that exist: _record_stage_timings already records release_seconds, waits_seconds and launch_seconds per pass (service.py:145-170), and selection.py:305 is the whole-order loop with no deadline, so the two deliverables are one instrument (a clock and an interruption on the existing loop, plus a finer stage split), not a new timer beside it.

findings.reason: the endpoint is one bounded pass that reports its own cadence; the design must end the pass through one exit that settles its result, or a bounded pass returns a result with its verdict set half recorded.
findings.text: §6 and §7 both land inside the `for index, pointer in enumerate(order)` loop at selection.py:305-751, which today iterates the entire order with no deadline and has nine `continue` exits each following its own remaining/verdicts bookkeeping. A budget check, a role share and a per-launch timer threaded through those nine paths is three shallow edits to the branch-densest function in the package, and any new early exit skips the bookkeeping that follows it.

findings.reason: a node briefed from §5 as written can build a parallel queue path; the plan should say one existing gate widens.
findings.text: §5's "stored as a queued request exactly as a held local dispatch is" is already the shape of the code: the roster refusal is caught at preparation.py:1027-1040 and the queue write follows at :1051-1053 behind `is_local and not shadow_lineage`, and a metered lane's budget hold queues at :665-703. The change is to widen those two `is_local` gates (:1027, :1052); a second queue path beside them is a wrapper with no justification.

findings.reason: the package is contradictory, so §5 must settle it or the node will diffuse a behaviour change a message already promises.
findings.text: the roster refusal already tells the caller "A request queued behind this cap launches then" while preparation.py:1027 only queues for `is_local`, so the message and the behaviour disagree today for every non-local lane; §5 should state which of the two moves rather than leave a node to pick.

rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 re-implements interleaving that weighted_project_order owns at reckon/crew/admission/ordering.py:70, and §8 a fleet census that queued_placements (ordering.py:192) and open_run_index.read_rows (open_run_index.py:397) own.
